The findings highlighted disparities in awareness and willingness to use PrEP among different racial groups. 2. Wingood et al. (2013) conducted a national survey to explore racial differences and correlates of potential PrEP adoption. The results, published in JAIDS, emphasized the need for targeted interventions to address these disparities. 3. A presentation at the 7th IAS Conference on HIV Pathogenesis and Treatment (2013) discussed participant motivations for enrolling and continuing in the FEM-PrEP HIV prevention clinical trial. The study provided insights into factors influencing trial participation. 4. A study published in PLOS ONE (2013) investigated the acceptability of PrEP among men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women in Northern Thailand. The findings revealed varying levels of acceptability and highlighted the importance of addressing cultural and social factors. 5. Research published in PLOS ONE (2014) examined the interest in PrEP among female sex workers in Guangxi, China. The study identified barriers and facilitators to PrEP uptake in this population. 6. A study in the International Journal of STD and AIDS (2013) explored the acceptability of antiretrovirals for HIV prevention among vulnerable communities. The findings underscored the challenges and opportunities in promoting PrEP in these groups. 7. A qualitative study published in BMJ Open (2014) identified barriers to PrEP uptake and use among communities most affected by HIV in Scotland. The research provided valuable insights into the social and structural factors influencing PrEP adoption. 8. A study in PLOS ONE (2013) assessed awareness and willingness to use PrEP among gay and bisexual men in Scotland. The findings highlighted the implications for biomedical HIV prevention strategies. 9. Research published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs (2013) examined attitudes toward PrEP among MSM in Western China. The study identified key factors influencing PrEP acceptability in this population. 10. A presentation at the 19th International AIDS Conference (2012) discussed factors associated with willingness to use oral PrEP among MSM in Shenyang, China. The study provided insights into the determinants of PrEP uptake. 11. A study in the Journal of Zhejiang University (2011) explored the acceptability of PrEP among female sex workers in Xinjiang, China. The findings highlighted the need for tailored interventions to promote PrEP in this population. 12. Research published in the Academic Journal of Second Military Medical University (2012) examined attitudes toward PrEP among drug users from high-risk populations in Western China. The study identified barriers and facilitators to PrEP adoption. 13. A study in PLOS ONE (2012) assessed the willingness to accept PrEP among Chinese MSM. The findings provided valuable insights into the factors influencing PrEP uptake in this group. 14. Matthews et al. (2012) reviewed the use of antiretrovirals for safer conception among HIV-serodiscordant couples. The study, published in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS, highlighted the role of antiretrovirals in reducing HIV transmission risk during conception. 15. Young et al. (2014) conducted a review of research on the acceptability of oral PrEP and treatment as prevention for sexually transmitted HIV. The findings, published in AIDS and Behavior, emphasized the importance of understanding user preferences and values. 16. A systematic review and meta-analysis (2015) examined the use of oral PrEP for individuals at substantial risk of HIV infection. The study provided evidence-based recommendations for PrEP implementation. 17. Kennedy et al. (2014) reviewed the values and preferences of MSM and transgender individuals regarding PrEP. The findings highlighted the importance of addressing community-specific needs in PrEP programs. 18. Kennedy et al. (2012) conducted a review of the values and preferences of serodiscordant couples regarding PrEP. The study emphasized the need for tailored interventions to support PrEP use in this population. 19. Schneiders (2014) conducted a qualitative study on the values and preferences of transgender individuals regarding PrEP. The findings provided insights into the unique needs of this population. 20. Henderson et al. (2014) summarized the values and preferences of key populations, including people who inject drugs, regarding HIV prevention and harm reduction strategies. The report emphasized the importance of community engagement in PrEP programs. 21. A consultation by INPUD and UNAIDS (2014) focused on the perspectives of people who inject drugs regarding PrEP. The meeting report highlighted the challenges and opportunities in promoting PrEP in this population. 22. A global consultation (2014) explored the experiences and perspectives of sex workers regarding PrEP and early treatment as HIV prevention strategies. The findings emphasized the need for community-driven approaches. 23. The Global Forum on MSM and HIV (2014) conducted a qualitative study on the values and preferences of MSM regarding the use of antiretroviral therapy as prevention. The study provided insights into the acceptability of PrEP in this population. 24. The World Health Organization (2015) published a comprehensive report summarizing the values and preferences of various populations regarding PrEP. The report emphasized the importance of addressing social and structural barriers to PrEP uptake.
